bright-angel-indian-garden.note: The National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated September 14, 2026, now describes Bright Angel Trail as open from the trailhead down to River Resthouse, farther than the previously reported Havasupai Gardens cutoff; the trail remains closed below that point except for river-trip exchanges at Pipe Creek Beach (Source: National Park Service). This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river crossing bridges; the park states recovery is ongoing with no estimated reopening at this time for the closed sections. Stage 4 water restrictions remain in effect; most inner canyon water sources are off, though South Kaibab Trailhead water remains on. Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk. Confirm the current endpoint with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending past Havasupai Gardens. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, reconfirmed unchanged today on the NPS Key Hiking Messages page, last updated September 14, 2026 (Source: National Park Service). Phantom Ranch reservations remain cancelled and Colorado River traffic through the area remains halted. Park recovery crews continue infrastructure assessment and repair work, including a temporary water intake at Bright Angel Creek. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
